era: Arcade / Master System / Genesis / Game Gear / Saturn / PlayStation 3 / Xbox 360
summary: Sega's fantasy beat-'em-up series, including arcade originals, Genesis sequels, handheld/RPG spin-offs, a Saturn fighting game, and Beast Rider.

entries.title: Golden Axe
entries.definitive_edition: Genesis/Mega Drive version, supplemented by Master System and PC Engine CD curiosities

emulation.emulator: Genesis Plus GX / BlastEm / MiSTer; MAME for arcade supplement
emulation.notes: Use the Genesis/Mega Drive version for the main route; arcade emulation is only needed for purist visual comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Accurate Genesis/Mega Drive emulation plus arcade reference

primary.version: Genesis/Mega Drive version via modern collection or emulator
primary.why: The arcade game is the visual baseline, but the Genesis/Mega Drive version adds a new level, Duel mode, a new ending, and Death Bringer as the true final boss. That makes Genesis/Mega Drive the best complete main route, with Master System and PC Engine CD worth checking only for their exclusive alternate content/presentation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version through Sega Genesis Classics, original hardware, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, or BlastEm; then sample Master System/PC Engine CD extras if desired.

secondary.exclusive_content: Single-character Tarik retelling and altered design
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Master System version if you want its alternate Tarik-focused adaptation.
secondary.why: It is a substantially altered solo adaptation rather than the definitive main route.

secondary.exclusive_content: CD audio and anime-style animated cutscenes
secondary.what_to_play: Watch/sample the PC Engine CD presentation after the Genesis playthrough.
secondary.why: It has presentation extras but source-documented reduced color, no co-op, and gameplay compromises.

entries.title: Golden Axe: The Revenge of Death Adder

emulation.notes: Use original cabinet where possible, especially for four-player play.

primary.why: The Revenge of Death Adder is an arcade-only sequel with four playable characters, branching paths, and four-player support. It did not receive a conventional home port, though official mini/arcade hardware later included it.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original arcade board/cabinet or an official Astro City Mini/Arcade1Up route; use arcade emulation only with legally sourced ROMs.

all_releases.fidelity: Original arcade release with four-player support and branching routes.
all_releases.reason: primary: original and only full-scale release.

all_releases.fidelity: Official mini-cabinet/arcade reproduction route.
all_releases.reason: skip: practical official access route, but original arcade remains the fidelity baseline.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Original arcade remains the complete baseline; later mini routes are access methods.

entries.remaster_caveats: No conventional home port/remaster is known to exist.

primary.why: The Duel is a one-on-one fighting spin-off released in arcades and on Saturn. The Saturn version is documented as nearly arcade-perfect and adds a training mode, making it the best complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Saturn version on original hardware or a Saturn emulator such as Mednafen/Beetle Saturn.

entries.title: Golden Axe: Beast Rider

emulation.notes: Original hardware is the safest route; emulator compatibility should be checked before committing.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD seventh-generation console output, potentially higher via emulator

primary.why: Beast Rider released only on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 as a 3D action reboot starring Tyris Flare. No PC, remaster, or content-expanded edition is documented, so the two HD console versions are the complete release family.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 or Xbox 360 disc on original hardware; use RPCS3 or Xenia only if compatibility is acceptable.

all_releases.fidelity: Original seventh-generation console release.
all_releases.reason: primary: only documented release family.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No alternate edition with unique content is known to exist.

entries.remaster_caveats: No PC port or remaster is known to exist.
